current.text: He was traded from Milwaukee to Miami.
Miami lacks other ball handlers. He played basically as a point guard in Miami's first preseason game.
It is still open whether Miami starts a traditional point guard or lets him run point. Davion Mitchell may not close games.
Experts expect 32 to 33 minutes a game and high usage as Miami's main creator.
His assist rate should rise because no one else on Miami handles the ball.
Experts expect over 60 games, but not 70.
Experts are not very worried about last season's calf injuries and missed games, since some came while the Bucks were tanking. A new calf issue would be a concern.
Experts call him the clear 5th pick in category leagues and say he should not fall past pick 5.
Getting him at pick 6 to 8 is strong value.
Experts call his ESPN rank of about 20 egregious. At worst he is a top 9 player.
An expert prices him at about 60 USD in auctions. He went for 58 USD in a mock, about where he should sit.
With more minutes and aggression his FG% could get back to 65%.
Miami has the league-fewest 13 back-to-backs and none in the fantasy playoffs.
Nothing points to him sitting back-to-backs. He may sit one or two.
With the March 28 end, Miami plays 4, 3 and 3 games in weeks 19 to 21, 10 games in total.
The expert calls Miami's playoff schedule weak.
The East is very stacked, so Miami may not be able to coast and rest players for long stretches.

durable.text: He is an elite FG% source on high volume, around 61 to 62% on 18 to 19 attempts a game.
He shoots about 65% from the line on high volume, the worst FT impact in the league.
He will probably stay a bad free throw shooter, though a random 70% season would not be crazy.
Drafting him points to a punt FT% build. Do not chase free throws around him.
He makes very few threes and is not a good shooter from deep.
Threes are easy to recover elsewhere, so drafting him does not mean punting three categories.
He commits many turnovers, a negative in our TO category.
He is a top scorer and double-digit rebounder with guard-like assists for a forward.
His steals and blocks have declined steadily from his peak.
Experts are not sure his steals and blocks will come back.
He has a long injury history, with persistent knee problems and calf injuries last season.
Plain 9-cat rankings undervalue him because of his free throws. His real H2H impact is huge, and punting a category is viable.
Experts list his age as a concern.

note: Experts call him a clear top 5 pick in category leagues. Yahoo values him at 55 USD with an average cost of 60.8 USD, he went for 62 USD in our auction last season, and an expert puts him at about 60 USD, so plan to spend around 60 to 62 USD. ESPN's rank of 19 is widely called too low. If you buy him, build around punting FT% and accept the turnovers. In return you get elite FG%, points, rebounds and assists from a forward. Early in the season, check that he gets the 32 to 33 minutes experts expect, that he handles the ball, and that his calf stays healthy. Miami's weak 4-3-3 playoff schedule (10 games) is a small minus, but the team has no back-to-backs in those weeks.
